small_guidance:
- The GEMM uses `allow_tf32=False`, forcing slow fp32 mma. Switch to `allow_tf32=True` (or convert inputs to tf32/fp16 path) — this alone should roughly halve the GEMM time on the 4090.
- Drop the explicit `Bt = weight.t().contiguous()` materialization and instead pass `weight` with swapped strides (stride_bk=weight.stride(1), stride_bn=weight.stride(0)); saves a full 8192x8192 transpose copy on every forward.
- Add a `GROUP_M` swizzle (e.g. 8) to the GEMM and broaden autotune with `BLOCK_M=128,BLOCK_N=256,BLOCK_K=64,num_warps=8,num_stages=3/4` configs tuned for M=1024,N=K=8192.
large_guidance:
- Redesign as a two-kernel pipeline where GEMM writes directly in a layout friendly to GroupNorm: keep output as (M, G, C_per_G) contiguous along C_per_G=512, so the GN kernel does one row-group per program with vectorized 512-wide loads, then fuse hardtanh in epilogue (already done). Avoid re-reading 32MB through global memory by chaining via L2-resident tiles only if persistent; otherwise just minimize re-traffic.
- Consider splitting GEMM by N into G column-panels (one panel per group, N=512 wide) and fusing the GroupNorm reduction at the tail of the GEMM: each program emits a (BLOCK_M, 512) tile that is exactly one (row, group), so mean/var can be reduced locally in registers without a separate kernel. This removes one full HBM round-trip of the 32MB activation.
- For the GEMM itself, use tf32 `tl.dot` (4090 has fast tf32 tensor cores) and tile (128,128,32) with `num_stages=4`; current fp32-mma path is the dominant bottleneck.
